fig1_schottky_anomaly.svg: Two-level system $\{0,\varepsilon\}$ vs reduced temperature $kT/\varepsilon$, from two_level_energy and two_level_heat_capacity. The mean energy (blue) climbs from 0 to $\varepsilon/2$ as the levels equalise; the heat capacity (orange) vanishes at both extremes and peaks near $kT\approx0.42\,\varepsilon$ -- the Schottky anomaly. Only a partly-excited gap can absorb heat.
fig2_einstein_heat_capacity.svg: Heat capacity of one quantum (Einstein) oscillator vs $T/\Theta_E$, from einstein_heat_capacity. Below the Einstein temperature $\Theta_E=\hbar\omega/k$ the gap freezes the mode out and $C\to0$; well above it every quadratic degree of freedom is thermally active and $C/k\to1$, the classical Dulong-Petit value (dashed).
